title: Not faith alone as opposed to other virtues; other acts also dispose
source_text: XLVIII. Verum quod fidei hac in parte tribuunt, reliquis quoque virtutibus Christianis convenire putant, & operibus ex gratia Dei factis. Itaque fidem solam si praecise consideretur, & prout virtutibus aliis opponitur, justificare negant. Nam sicut, ex eorum doctrina, fidei actus hominem disponit ad consequendam a Deo gratiam justificationis, & eatenus illum justificare dicitur, ita quoque timor judicii divini, peccati odium & detestatio, spes misericordiae, propositum vitae emendandae, inchoata Dei dilectio, & actus alii similes, ad veram poenitentiam & conversionem ad Deum requisiti, sunt dispositiones, ex ordinatione divina, necessariae ut aliquis a Deo remissionem peccatorum impetret, & habituali justitia donetur. Ac quemadmodum fidei habitus pars est justitiae, quam Deus in justificatione peccatori infundit, sic quoque partes illius sunt habitus spei, & charitatis: nec constat illa sola fide, sed virtutibus Christianis omnibus. Adeoque ex eorum sensu, virtutes reliquae, non minus quam fides, pertinent ad causam formalem justificationis, & bona multa opera, quae cum fidei actu justificationem peccatoris praecedunt, non minus quam actus ille, justificant per modum dispositionis.
pass_a_gloss: But what they attribute to faith in this part they think also belongs to the remaining Christian virtues and to works done from God's grace. Therefore they deny that faith alone, if precisely considered and as opposed to other virtues, justifies. For just as, on their doctrine, the act of faith disposes a man to obtain from God the grace of justification, and so far is said to justify him, so also fear of divine judgment, hatred and detestation of sin, hope of mercy, purpose of amending life, begun love of God, and other like acts required for true repentance and conversion to God, are dispositions, by divine ordinance, necessary that someone obtain from God remission of sins and be gifted with habitual righteousness. And just as the habit of faith is a part of the righteousness which God infuses into the sinner in justification, so also its parts are the habits of hope and charity: nor does that righteousness consist in faith alone, but in all the Christian virtues. And so on their sense the remaining virtues, no less than faith, pertain to the formal cause of justification, and many good works which with the act of faith precede the sinner's justification, no less than that act, justify by way of disposition.
pass_b_english: Rome denies faith alone if opposed to other virtues: fear, hatred of sin, hope, resolve, love also dispose.
Infused righteousness = faith + hope + charity habits, not faith alone.

choices.why: Other repentant acts share faith's disposing role.
rejected: works as condign meritorious cause of first grace
